evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52 h = 12.03 mg/L, far above 2.0 mg/L minimum; no oxygen stress
Receiving P(48h)=2.84 g/L matches source-1/2/3 at 48h (3.06/3.02/2.98 g/L) - normal trajectory
Source batches show P declining after ~72-76 h peak (8.36->6.85, 8.21->7.00, 8.02->6.43 g/L by 96 h), motivating reduced dilution/loss
Forward model KEEP: 576.3 kg, min DO2 8.53 mg/L; reduce_feed: 595.5 kg, min DO2 10.34 mg/L; both feasible 5/5 sensitivity members
Source DO2 dips to ~8.5 mg/L mid-run and recovers; receiving shows same pattern, so feed reduction poses no DO risk
args.rationale: Batch is on a normal trajectory (P at 48h = 2.84 g/L matching source; DO2 ~12 mg/L, no oxygen constraint). Source history and the source-calibrated forward model both indicate product mass peaks mid-cycle and decays/dilutes toward 96 h. A bounded 20% feed reduction reduces dilution and late-cycle loss, raising predicted product mass from ~576 to ~596 kg while increasing the DO2 minimum from ~8.5 to ~10.3 mg/L, feasible across all sensitivity members. Stronger cuts were rejected as unnecessary model-trust risk; stop is zero production.
args.uncertainty: Model is source-calibrated and the hidden receiving realization may differ; the predicted ~3% mass gain could shrink or reverse, and actual receiving kinetics could respond differently to reduced feed. Downside is limited because DO2 margin is large (~12 vs 2 mg/L) and no feasibility risk was found in any sensitivity member. No extra assay requested because a 4-h-turnaround assay would not change the bounded, low-risk choice.
